newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars end steady, await U.S. elections.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars end steady, await U.S. elections.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ended little changed in thin trade on Monday as players adjusted their positions ahead of the U.S. Presidential election on Tuesday.
Dealers said President Bill Clinton was widely expected to be re-elected but the market was increasingly focused on the Congressional races.

"If the Democrats win, there's talk it would be negative for U.S. treasuries. A Democratic president and a Democratic Congress would probably delay the passing of a balanced budget," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
He said March Eurodollars were likely to be well supported around 94.38 going into the election, with 94.45 capping their topside. They finished at 94.42, unchanged from their IMM close at 94.42.
The trader said a Democratic Congressional victory could cause a sell-off in U.S. stocks, which would in turn spur selling of U.S. treasuries.
"It wouldn't be immediate but they could come off quite a bit because they've had a good run up recently. March could even be knocked below 94.00," he added.

Euroyen futures scarcely moved all day as a holiday in Japan severely hampered interest on SIMEX. The lead June contract stood at 99.25 in late trade against its IMM close at 99.26. Turnover was a mere 336 lots.
Japanese government bond futures for December were not traded due to the holiday.
